item.title: Shenzhen, Asia-Pacific join hands for win-win outcomes
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Shenzhen, Asia-Pacific join hands for win-win outcomes Shenzhen, a coastal city in south China's Guangdong Province, is buzzing as it prepares to host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on Nov. 18-19, welcoming guests from across the Asia-Pacific. An APEC-themed banner hangs at a metro station in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 14. (People's Daily Online/Wang Xing) Foreign tourists wait to collect their luggage at Shenzhen Bao'an International Airport in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 19. (People's Daily Online/Ha Jung-mi) "We should stay true to the vision of harmony without uniformity, fully leverage the diversity of Asia Pacific economies, draw on each other's strengths, and jointly make the pie of Asia Pacific cooperation bigger. We should advance both our respective interests and those of others, and foster an environment of cooperation to achieve success and development for all economies," Chinese President Xi Jinping said in a written address at the APEC CEO Summit in Gyeongju, South Korea, in October 2025. China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for the 2026 APEC "China Year." Cooperation means drawing on each member's strengths, aligning policies and sharing experience. Shenzhen's comparative advantages lie in its comprehensive electronics industry chain and vibrant innovation ecosystem. The robot block in Bantian, Longgang district, offers a case in point. The world's first robot 6S store and AI 6S store stand side by side there. Overseas makers can turn ideas into products at the block, with services covering design, prototyping, customization and incubation. Humanoid robots perform outside the world's first robot 6S store in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, during an activity for the 2026 APEC "China Year," drawing Chinese and foreign tourists, Oct. 21, 2026. (People's Daily Online/Andrew Smith) "We hope to share Shenzhen's complete industrial support system with APEC partners," said Zhou Fangzheng, executive store manager of the robot 6S store. More than 300 companies working in humanoid and specialized robotics have gathered at the store. Since its opening, the store has received visits from executives from LG Group and Procter & Gamble, and several organizations from Malaysia and Singapore have expressed interest in cooperation. The AI 6S store has attracted more than 350 partners, showcased over 600 AI products and received 300,000 visits, over 30 percent from overseas, since opening in September last year, said deputy manager Yu Fang. A popular robot duck, Microduck, developed by a team from the world's largest AI open source community, was brought to market with the help of Shenzhen's supply chain. Longgang is home to more than 800 companies in the AI industry chain, 12,700 robot-related companies and more than 2,500 industrial enterprises above designated size, providing a strong foundation for supply chain collaboration across the Asia-Pacific. Shenzhen's ties with the Asia-Pacific go beyond industrial collaboration and extend to deeper institutional cooperation. On July 26, 2026, the International Mangrove Center, the world's first intergovernmental organization exclusively dedicated to mangrove protection, held its first council meeting in Shenzhen and began full operations. It has 21 signatory countries, including nine members. The center has contributed to global ecological governance, holding six international workshops attended by 137 representatives from 30 countries. At the APEC Ministerial Meeting on Forestry on July 27 and 28, heads of delegations from 21 APEC economies planted mangrove seedlings at Shenzhen Museum of Contemporary Art and Urban Planning. The seedlings will later be transplanted to the "APEC Forestry Ministers' Forest" at the Futian Mangrove National Nature Reserve. Seedlings for the "APEC Forestry Ministers' Forest" at the Futian Mangrove National Nature Reserve in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 19. (People's Daily Online/Zhou Jielu) Art has become a bridge for people-to-people exchanges in the Asia-Pacific. At the Guanlan Original Printmaking Base, artists from around the world create side by side. German artist Ute Wöllmann painted two lines from a poem by ancient Chinese poet Li Bai alongside two lines by a German poet. The base has welcomed more than 2,000 overseas artists since it opened. German artist Ute Wöllmann introduces her works created at the Guanlan Original Printmaking Base in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Oct. 20. (People's Daily Online/Shen Yuhuan) The Shenzhen SME Going Global Service Reception Hall at the Longgang Enterprise Internationalization Service Base in Longgang district has created a platform to connect supply and demand among small and medium-sized enterprises across the Asia-Pacific. The base has served 9,494 companies seeking to expand overseas and released orders worth more than 13.5 billion yuan (about $2.02 billion). Photo taken on Oct. 21 shows a digital screen at the Shenzhen SME Going Global Service Reception Hall in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (People's Daily Online/Shen Yuhuan) "The APEC meeting provides a valuable channel of communication between Shenzhen and Asia-Pacific economies. We look forward to more practical cooperation dividends from the meeting," said Li Qun, deputy general manager of Shenzhen Longgang Industrial Investment Service Group Co., Ltd. In the first three quarters of this year, Shenzhen's imports and exports with other APEC economies reached 3.23 trillion yuan, accounting for nearly 70 percent of the city's total foreign trade. item.title: Shenzhen offers glimpse into Asia-Pacific energy cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
China Focus: Shenzhen offers glimpse into Asia-Pacific energy cooperation SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- At the press center for the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week in Shenzhen, a large screen displays real-time data on the amount of green electricity powering the event and the carbon emissions avoided as a result. During the event, key venues, transport hubs, and reception facilities are running on 100 percent green electricity. The electricity can be partly traced to offshore wind farms within south China's Guangdong Province, where Shenzhen is located, and partly to wind and solar bases in remote "desert, Gobi and barren land" regions in northwest China, among other sources. As the 2026 APEC "China Year" is nearing its culmination, energy cooperation has emerged as one of its most tangible areas of progress. Moreover, APEC economies account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and about 60 percent of global energy demand, making the region central to the global energy landscape. Shenzhen, as the host city and a major innovation hub, offers a window into China's vision for an "Asia-Pacific Energy Community," a concept proposed and systematically defined for the first time in a joint statement issued at the 16th APEC Energy Ministerial Meeting held in September in Beijing. From low-carbon venues to daily conservation practices, the city provides tangible clues to understanding this vision. At a garbage incineration park in the city's Nanshan District, municipal waste is transformed into electricity. The facility incinerates about 2,300 tonnes of waste each day, equivalent to about one-eighth of Shenzhen's daily total, converting heat into around 1.4 million kilowatt-hours of clean electricity per day. This "Shenzhen solution" is now being adapted for other Asia-Pacific economies, including Thailand and Malaysia. Wang Kai, technological head of the Nanshan Energy Ecological Park, noted that Chinese teams have tailored the technology to local conditions, such as extending fermentation periods to handle higher moisture content in local waste and recycling incineration slag into building bricks. Beyond garbage-to-electricity conversion, new energy vehicles rolling off production lines in Shenzhen, such as those produced by BYD, have powered the global shift toward electric mobility. Moreover, Chinese firms are involved in energy conservation infrastructure construction in other countries in the Asia-Pacific region. Guangdong-based China Southern Power Grid is taking part in a high-voltage direct current transmission project in Chile. Once completed, it will transmit clean wind and solar power from the Atacama Desert to load centers, helping resolve the mismatch between renewable generation and consumption. Zhang Jingjia, an associate researcher at Nankai University's APEC research center, said the Asia-Pacific Energy Community will help forge connectivity across power grids, renewable energy supply chains, and AI-enabled energy systems. Beyond cooperation initiatives, China's growing clean energy manufacturing capacity in general is helping lower the cost of green technologies and expand their availability worldwide. According to the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA), over the past decade, global wind and solar power costs have fallen by more than 60 percent and 80 percent, respectively, with much of this attributed to China's innovation, manufacturing and engineering endeavors. China's growing contribution to global clean energy development is underpinned by the rapid transformation of its own energy system. In July 2026, China's installed solar capacity, for the first time in its history, overtook coal-fired capacity, making solar its largest power source by installed capacity. "China is ready to work with all economies to turn our shared consensus into concrete action, transform our experience into collaboration, and jointly build an inclusive, innovative, and synergized Asia-Pacific energy community," said Wang Jianbo, deputy director of the National Energy Administration. item.title: Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Carney is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Canada to further advance their new strategic partnership, he added. Xi said China and Canada should build on the current momentum to enhance political mutual trust and steadily build the right perception of each other's development path and policy intent, deepen understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and settle differences and disagreements. The two countries should better align efforts to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade, energy, agriculture and finance, and expand cooperation in emerging areas including the green economy, e-commerce and the digital economy, in order to better harness each other's strengths and achieve win-win outcomes, he said. He called for deeper people-to-people exchanges and more exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, tourism, science, technology and youth as well as at subnational levels. He also proposed closer coordination to jointly practice true multilateralism, uphold the authority of the United Nations and the multilateral trading system, and build a more just and equitable global governance system. Carney said that bilateral relations have been on the right track of development since the launch of the Canada-China new strategic partnership during his meeting with Xi early this year. The two countries can fully advance and deepen cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, Carney said. Canada will work with China to pursue stronger cooperation in trade, investment, new energy, agricultural products, artificial intelligence, tourism and other areas, reduce the list of irritants, and expand the list of cooperation, he said. Canada stands ready to strengthen coordination with China to advance cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, uphold multilateralism, promote free trade, and contribute to stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region and the world, Carney added. item.title: Xi says to boost China-Papua New Guinea ties to new heights
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Xi says to boost China-Papua New Guinea ties to new heights Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea (PNG) to enhance political mutual trust and strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, advancing the development of bilateral relations to new heights. China has always regarded PNG as a trustworthy good friend and good partner, Xi said while meeting with PNG Prime Minister James Marape in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Marape is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that the PNG government adheres to the one-China principle and takes concrete actions to support China's efforts to safeguard territorial integrity and national reunification, Xi said it is a just act in keeping with the trend of history. Xi stressed that China stands ready to work with PNG to strengthen exchanges on governance and development experience, better synergize high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and PNG's Connect PNG Program and other strategies, and deepen cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, agriculture and fisheries, and energy and minerals. China is also ready to explore new avenues of cooperation in the digital economy, financial services, green energy, science and technology to help PNG achieve sustainable development, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen coordination within multilateral fora such as the United Nations and the APEC, uphold international fairness and justice, expand cooperation in tackling climate change and protecting the marine environment, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi noted. China is a good friend and the most important partner of PNG, Marape said. Over the past 50 years of diplomatic ties, PNG has consistently adhered to the one-China principle, firmly supported China in safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and resolutely backed China's efforts to achieve national reunification and advance national rejuvenation. PNG highly appreciates China's important role in guiding international affairs, supports the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi Jinping, and stands ready to strengthen multilateral coordination with China to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and promote prosperity and stability in the Asia-Pacific region, he said. item.title: Xi says China-Vietnam top-level exchanges inject positive energy into regional peace, development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Xi says China-Vietnam top-level exchanges inject positive energy into regional peace, development General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday met with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. In recent years, the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries have maintained close exchanges and reached important consensus on building a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance, Xi said. This has helped advance bilateral relations and injected positive energy into regional peace and development, Xi added. The Vietnamese leader is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi expressed willingness to deepen experience sharing with Vietnam, firmly support each other, and strengthen exchanges on self-supervision and self-governance of the parties, so as to ensure continuous progress in both countries' socialist causes and national development. "As comrades and brothers, China and Vietnam must stand together and weather the storms," Xi said. Xi also underscored the importance of enhancing mutual trust and solidarity, deepening all-round cooperation, jointly safeguarding peace and stability, and advancing shared development and prosperity. The two sides should properly manage maritime differences and steadily advance maritime cooperation, Xi said. Xi called on China and Vietnam to strengthen coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation and Lancang-Mekong cooperation, and to fulfill their duties as successive hosts of APEC in 2026 and 2027, respectively. Noting that the Vietnamese side views China as its most important strategic support, Lam said that, amid the current complex international situation, his country stands ready to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to support the development of both countries. Lam also pledged to work with China to safeguard maritime stability. As the next APEC host, Vietnam will build on the outcomes of APEC "China Year" and continue efforts to advance Asia-Pacific cooperation, the Vietnamese leader added. item.title: Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that he is ready to work with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast to strengthen strategic guidance, keep to the right direction, and jointly draw a blueprint for the growth of bilateral relations, so as to support the development and prosperity of the two countries. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with Kast in Shenzhen. The Chilean president is in the southern Chinese city to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. The most valuable experience is that the two sides respect each other, treat each other as equals, and pursue win-win outcomes, he said. As this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Chile comprehensive strategic partnership and the 20th anniversary of the entry into force of the China-Chile Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral relations have reached an important juncture for building on past achievements and forging ahead into the future, Xi said. item.title: Commentary: For APEC, the answer lies in action
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Commentary: For APEC, the answer lies in action An APEC-themed installation is seen on Xiangmihu road in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 15, 2026. The 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19. The city has been adorned with flowers and lush greenery, with APEC elements integrated into the cityscape. (Xinhua/Deng Hua) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Twelve years after last hosting APEC, China is once again taking the helm, with a clear mission to turn the long-standing vision of an Asia-Pacific community into concrete action. That mission has become more pressing as geopolitical tensions mount, protectionism surges, and global economic cooperation faces growing headwinds. Against this backdrop, the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19 in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, will bring together the 21 member economies to address common challenges, deepen regional cooperation and chart a path toward prospering together. It offers an opportunity to inject much-needed certainty and confidence into the global economy. For decades, the Asia-Pacific has been one of the world's most dynamic engines of growth, fueled by expanding trade, investment, industrial cooperation and cross-border connectivity. Today, the 21 APEC member economies are home to about 40 percent of the world's population, and account for more than 60 percent of global GDP and nearly half of global trade, underscoring the region's central role in the global economy. The deeper the economic ties, the greater the need for cooperation and a shared vision for the future. APEC has consistently championed the vision of an Asia-Pacific community, recognizing that the region's future lies in openness, integration and mutual benefit. But the foundations of this prosperity are now under strain. Unilateralism, trade barriers and attempts to fragment industrial and supply chains are threatening to reverse the trend of economic integration. In an interconnected global economy, decoupling and confrontation will only drive up costs, erode confidence and constrain opportunities. This makes the vision of an Asia-Pacific community more relevant than ever. But a shared vision, however compelling, cannot sustain itself on rhetoric. For decades, the goal of building an Asia-Pacific community has been reiterated time and again, yet translating it into action remains a formidable task. Against this backdrop, three priorities for the 2026 APEC "China Year" -- openness, innovation and cooperation -- speak directly to the challenges facing the Asia-Pacific. These are not slogans but imperatives for sustaining growth in the region. Openness is the lifeblood of Asia-Pacific prosperity. More than three decades ago, APEC was born amid a new wave of economic globalization. Since its inception, the group has championed the liberalization and facilitation of trade and investment, helping transform the Asia-Pacific into one of the world's major engines of economic growth. By opening markets, removing barriers, aligning rules and building platforms for cooperation, China has become the largest trading partner of 13 APEC economies. Eight APEC members are among China's top 10 trading partners, while China contributes more than 60 percent of the region's economic growth. Innovation is the driving force behind Asia-Pacific prosperity. AI and the digital economy have been among the most widely discussed topics at events throughout China's APEC host year. The fruits of technological innovation, however, should be shared, not walled off or monopolized for the benefit of a select few. China has consistently taken concrete steps to ensure that the benefits of innovation deliver tangible results throughout the region. Cooperation is the bedrock of Asia-Pacific prosperity. APEC economies differ in their resource endowments and level of development, but by turning these differences into complementary strengths and shared opportunities, APEC can help developing economies build capacity for sustainable growth and ensure that no economy is left behind. The real test of the Shenzhen meeting will be whether the vision of an Asia-Pacific community translates into real action, from shaping non-binding rules and standards to advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, strengthening supply chain connectivity, and bridging the digital divide. Turning vision into reality requires sustained efforts from every APEC member. Over the past year, China has turned this shared vision into initiatives open to all economies. More than 300 meetings and activities, including senior officials' meetings and ministerial meetings, have been held across the country. These events covered issues ranging from the digital economy and green transition to supply chain resilience and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises. Shenzhen is a fitting venue for such a grand gathering. Once a small fishing village, it has grown into a global powerhouse in technology and advanced manufacturing, standing at the forefront of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. The city's trade with other APEC economies has grown more than tenfold in nearly three decades, surging from 267.5 billion yuan (about 40 billion U.S. dollars) in 1996 to 3.13 trillion yuan in 2025. With its GDP nearing 4 trillion yuan, Shenzhen is poised to become the third Chinese city to cross that threshold. Shenzhen's journey -- from embracing the international division of labor in the early days of reform and opening up, to becoming deeply integrated into global industrial and supply chains today -- is also testament to the Asia-Pacific's growth through exchanges, mutual learning and win-win cooperation. The transformation offers compelling evidence of how openness, innovation and cooperation can unlock tremendous potential. Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, China's third hosting of the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, 35 years after joining the organization, sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country's development need not come at the expense of another. Over the past three decades, APEC has served as a "regulator" of international relations, a "stabilizer" of the regional economic order and an "incubator" of new approaches to economic governance. One of APEC's greatest strengths is its ability to bridge differences and build consensus on thorny issues through dialogue and consultation. The Asia-Pacific region's experience demonstrates that integration and cooperation can generate opportunities far beyond what individual economies can achieve on their own. That experience should not be discarded at a time when the world needs it most. The more turbulent the waves, the greater the need for economies to row together. One meeting may not resolve all differences, but it can help build new consensus and set direction for future cooperation. As China enters its 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), its commitment to high-standard opening up carries far-reaching implications for the region. With APEC leaders gathering in Shenzhen, the world expects not just a shared vision, but also feasible measures that will be taken by all, benefit everyone, and ultimately stand the test of time.
